propositions: Mutated test code executing under mutmut run can perform arbitrary destructive filesystem operations (rm -rf) outside the source tree because source-tree isolation alone does not constrain runtime effects

Both the baseline pytest and mutmut run subprocesses in execute_shard() must be wrapped in OS-enforced sandboxes denying filesystem writes outside an explicit allow-list to prevent incident recurrence
Linux enforcement via bwrap must be verified functionally on Linux (not inferred from macOS results) to confirm write-deny works when unprivileged user namespaces are available

The sandbox mechanism must fail-closed: if no sandbox is available on a workstation, the run aborts non-zero; on CI runners the run may proceed unsandboxed with a WARNING, keyed to the CI environment variable

The enforcement tests must observe actual filesystem behavior (probe writes succeeding inside allow-list, failing outside, and rm -rf protected paths being denied) rather than only asserting on constructed sandbox argv
